name: spinner
title: Spinner
tagline: Equal-sector spinner (circle or polygon) with repeatable labels and a pointer; derives each angle and P(label)=matching÷total as a simplified fraction.
description: A divided spinner — the model for "P(land on X) by counting equal sectors". A circle, or a regular polygon (square, pentagon, hexagon, octagon), is split into equal sectors, one per label you give; labels may repeat (three "C" sectors out of eight), and a central pointer/needle sits over the figure. From the label list the model derives the number of sectors, each sector's equal angle (360 ÷ n), the dividing lines, the outline, one colour per distinct label (repeats share a hue so matching sectors are easy to count), the pointer, and — for any label you ask about — P(land on it) = matching sectors ÷ total as an exact simplified fraction, plus whether the spinner is fair (every label equally likely) or biased. Occlude a probability to ask for it; highlight a label to shade its sectors; point the needle at a sector to show a landed result. Distinct from pie-chart (whose sector angles are proportional to frequency, with no pointer and no repeated labels).
whenToUse: Reach for this for spinners in probability: a fair or biased spinner spun once, finding P(land on a colour / letter / number) by counting equal sectors, and the spinner stimulus that sits above a probability-scale, relative-frequency or sample-space question. Give "sectors" as the list of labels going clockwise from the top — the number of labels is the number of equal sectors, and repeats are simply repeated strings (["A","B","C","C","A","C","B","A"] is an 8-sector spinner with three Cs). Set "shape": "circle" for a round spinner, or "square" / "pentagon" / "hexagon" / "octagon" for a polygonal one — for a polygon give exactly as many labels as the shape has sides (square 4, pentagon 5, hexagon 6, octagon 8) so the dividing lines meet the corners. Every probability is derived — list the ones to display in "ask" as P(label) = matching ÷ total (simplified by default), occlude one to ask for it, highlight one to shade the sectors you are counting. Common configurations: worked example — ask each distinct label, show.simplified true. Answer space — omit "ask" and put the question in "caption" ("Write down P(an even number)"), so the figure is the stimulus a pupil answers from. Find the probability — one ask entry with occlude:true and highlight:true. Fair vs biased — show.fairness true adds a derived "fair" / "biased" line (fair when every label is equally likely). Landed result — pointer.at the sector the needle should point to (a spin outcome). Keep labels short (a letter, a number, a colour word): the model places a label outside on a leader line when its sector is too thin, but many long labels in many sectors will crowd, so prefer 8 sectors or fewer for word labels. Keep the same shape and the same show.* choices across a lesson so pupils read one consistent spinner. Switch model when the teaching changes — for parts of a whole as angles proportional to frequency use statistics/pie-chart; for the long-run frequency of many spins use probability/relative-frequency; for two combined events use statistics/sample-space-grid. Synonyms a teacher might use: spinner, fair spinner, biased spinner, spin, equally likely, equal sections, sectors, segments, probability, chance, likelihood, P(red), wheel.

items.description: One sector's label. Repeat a label to give it more than one sector — repeated labels share a colour and are counted together for probability.

sectors.description: The sector labels, going clockwise from the TOP sector. The COUNT of labels is the number of equal sectors (so this list alone fixes the geometry); every sector spans the same angle, 360 ÷ count. Labels may repeat: ["A","B","C","C","A","C","B","A"] is eight equal sectors, three of them "C". For a polygon shape give exactly as many labels as the shape has sides (square 4, pentagon 5, hexagon 6, octagon 8). Keep labels short — a letter, a number, or a colour word.

shape.description: The spinner outline. "circle" (default) is a round spinner with any 2–12 sectors. The polygons draw a flat-top regular shape whose corners the dividing lines meet — use as many sectors as the shape has sides: "square" 4, "pentagon" 5, "hexagon" 6, "octagon" 8. The sectors are still equal and the maths is identical to the circle; only the outline changes.

items.description: One probability to compute and show beneath the spinner, as "P(label) = matching ÷ total". List one entry per probability you want shown; omit the whole "ask" array for a pure stimulus (no readout) — the answer space a pupil works from.

label.description: The label whose probability to show. The model counts how many sectors carry EXACTLY this label and renders P = count ÷ total as an exact fraction (e.g. "P(C) = 3/8"). A label that appears on no sector gives P = 0 (an impossible event) — useful deliberately.

occlude.description: Render this probability's value as "?" — the question hook ("work out P(green)"). The spinner and its sectors stay fully visible; only the answer is hidden. Default false.

highlight.description: Amber every sector carrying this label AND this readout line — draws the eye to the sectors being counted (e.g. shade the four "Red" sectors while asking P(Red)). Default false.

ask.description: Which probabilities to display beneath the spinner. Each entry shows "P(label) = matching ÷ total" (simplified by default), derived by counting sectors. List one entry per distinct label you want shown (list them all for a full worked example); omit the array entirely for a pure stimulus with no readout. Occlude an entry to ask for its value; highlight an entry to shade the sectors it counts.

pointer.description: The central pointer/needle — the spinner's defining feature. Drawn by default, resting upright; set an outcome with "at" or "angle".

show.description: Draw the needle. Set false for a bare divided shape (e.g. "how many equal sections?"). Default true.

at.description: Point the needle at this sector — its number, counting from 1 at the TOP sector and going clockwise. Use to show a landed result ("the spinner landed here"). Out-of-range values are ignored and the needle rests upright.

angle.description: Point the needle at this angle in degrees, measured clockwise from straight up (0 = up, 90 = right). Ignored if "at" is given. Use for a needle resting between sectors. Default: straight up.

highlight.description: Amber the single sector the needle points at (the landed sector). Use with "at". Default false.

labels.description: Print each sector's label on the figure. Set false for an unlabelled divided shape. Default true.

fill.description: Tint each sector with its label's colour (one hue per distinct label; repeats share it). Set false for white sectors with just the outline and labels. Default true.

simplified.description: When a probability fraction reduces, also show the simplified form ("P(B) = 2/8 = 1/4"). Set false to show only matching ÷ total. Default true.

fairness.description: Add a derived line stating whether the spinner is FAIR (every label equally likely) or BIASED. Default false.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the figure, e.g. the context ("The spinner is spun once"). Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.
